title: Relief on a Car Rental Release Charge Where the Journey Has Fallen Away
content:
A rental on the Car Rental Rate Classes given up because the journey it was booked around has itself fallen away is relieved. Whether the journey has fallen away is read from the air booking the renter holds on the Air Ticket Fare Brands: the standing of that booking, and the form in which its value came back to the renter.

**The relief schedule.**

| The air booking the renter holds | Relieved at |
|---|---|
| Standing at cancelled or refunded, its value come back as a travel credit | 40 percent |
| Standing at cancelled or refunded, its value come back to the original form of payment | 20 percent |
| No such booking held | Nothing |

The relief is taken off the amount the release charge stands at when this relief is applied.

**Both parts of the condition.** Each of the first two entitlements requires the standing and the form of return together. A booking on the Air Ticket Fare Brands standing at cancelled whose value came back as a travel credit is relieved at 40 percent; standing at refunded with the same form of return, likewise 40 percent. Where the value came back to the original form of payment instead, the relief is 20 percent on either standing. Where the renter holds a booking on the Air Ticket Fare Brands that stands at neither cancelled nor refunded, no relief arises from it, whatever form of return it carries; and where the renter holds no such booking at all, no relief arises.

**Illustration on hypothetical holdings.** A renter giving up a car rental who holds an air booking standing at refunded, the value of which came back as a travel credit, is relieved at 40 percent. A renter holding an air booking standing at cancelled whose value came back to the card it was paid on is relieved at 20 percent. A renter holding a ticketed air booking still standing for travel is relieved at nothing.
